title: Jacob and Esau
illustrationStatus: Needs review before a playable release

discoveries.title: A Promise Continues
discoveries.narration: Abraham dies at 175 years old. Isaac and Ishmael bury their father, and Jehovah continues to bless Isaac. Abraham's life has ended, but Jehovah's promise hasn't.

interaction.prompt: Put these moments in the order the Bible gives them.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Every event is a labeled button; no dragging required.

progressiveHints.text: Start with Abraham's death, not his burial.
Both sons took part in the burial.
Genesis 25:11 tells us Jehovah blessed Isaac afterward.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 25:7–11 describes Abraham's death, his burial by Isaac and Ishmael, and Jehovah's continued blessing on Isaac.

discoveries.title: Rebekah Asks Jehovah
discoveries.narration: Rebekah is expecting twins, but their movements trouble her. She asks Jehovah what is happening. His answer shows that these two boys will matter far beyond their own household.

hotspots.label: Rebekah asks Jehovah about her pregnancy
Jehovah tells her two nations are involved
The older will serve the younger
An angel tells Rebekah to settle in Egypt

interaction.prompt: Which details really belong in this Bible account?
interaction.accessibleAlternative: All details can be selected as labeled buttons.

progressiveHints.text: What did Rebekah do when she was troubled?
Jehovah's answer concerned two peoples.
Choose Rebekah's question, two nations, and the older serving the younger.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 25:22, 23 tells us Rebekah inquired of Jehovah. He revealed that the two sons would become two peoples and that the older would serve the younger.

discoveries.title: Two Brothers, Different Lives
discoveries.narration: When the twins grow up, Esau becomes a skilled hunter who spends time in the field. Jacob is described as a blameless man who lives in tents. The brothers lead very different lives.

right.label: A skilled hunter, a man of the field
A blameless man dwelling in tents
He loved Esau because of the game he ate

interaction.prompt: Connect the details that belong together.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Each pair can be selected using labeled buttons.

progressiveHints.text: Genesis 25:27 describes both brothers.
One brother hunts, while the other is known for living in tents.
Genesis 25:28 says which son Isaac loved.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 25:27, 28 describes each brother and records the parents' preferences.

discoveries.title: A Meal and a Birthright
discoveries.narration: Esau comes home from the field exhausted, and Jacob has been making stew. Jacob asks Esau for his right as firstborn. Esau agrees, eats the lentil stew, and walks away. That's a very costly meal!

cards.label: Esau returns from the field exhausted
Esau swears and sells his birthright
Jacob gives Esau bread and lentil stew

interaction.prompt: Put these moments in the order the Bible gives them.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Every event is a labeled button; no dragging required.

progressiveHints.text: Esau's hunger begins the exchange.
Jacob asks for something far more important than a meal.
Esau swears before he eats the bread and stew.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 25:29–34 records Esau selling his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. The Bible says Esau despised the birthright.

discoveries.title: Isaac Faces a Famine
discoveries.narration: A famine strikes, and Isaac travels to Gerar. Jehovah tells him not to go down to Egypt and repeats the promise given to Abraham. Isaac stays in the land Jehovah directs him to live in.

hotspots.label: There is a famine in the land
Jehovah tells Isaac not to go to Egypt
Jehovah repeats the promise of blessing
Isaac moves his household to Egypt

interaction.prompt: Which details really belong in this Bible account?
interaction.accessibleAlternative: All details can be selected as labeled buttons.

progressiveHints.text: The account begins with a shortage of food.
Jehovah told Isaac where to stay.
Do not choose a move to Egypt; Jehovah told him not to go there.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 26:1–6 describes the famine, Jehovah's direction to Isaac, and the promise that all nations would receive a blessing through his offspring.

discoveries.title: The Wells of Gerar
discoveries.narration: Isaac prospers, but some of his neighbors begin to envy him. They stop up wells dug in Abraham's day. Even after fresh wells lead to quarrels, Isaac keeps moving and digging until his servants find water without another dispute.

cards.label: Isaac prospers, and the Philistines envy him
Wells from Abraham's day are stopped up
Isaac's servants dig wells that people dispute
At Rehoboth there is no quarrel over the new well

interaction.prompt: Put these moments in the order the Bible gives them.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Every event is a labeled button; no dragging required.

progressiveHints.text: The troubles start after Isaac becomes prosperous.
The blocked wells are followed by arguments over new ones.
The final well in this sequence is called Rehoboth.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 26:12–22 describes Isaac's prosperity, the wells stopped up by the Philistines, disputes over water, and a well Isaac named Rehoboth.

discoveries.title: Peace After the Disputes
discoveries.narration: At Beer-sheba, Jehovah reassures Isaac. Isaac builds an altar there. Later, Abimelech arrives with companions to make an agreement, and Isaac's servants bring good news: they've found water!

cards.label: Abimelech and his companions come to make an agreement
Isaac's servants report they have found water

interaction.prompt: Put these moments in the order the Bible gives them.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Every event is a labeled button; no dragging required.

progressiveHints.text: Read Genesis 26:23–25 for the first two moments.
The visitors arrive after Isaac builds the altar.
The news about the well comes after the agreement.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 26:23–33 tells us about Jehovah's reassurance, Isaac's altar, the peaceful agreement, and a newly found well.

discoveries.title: A Blessing and a Disguise
discoveries.narration: Isaac has grown old, and his eyesight is weak. He sends Esau to hunt and prepare food. Rebekah overhears him and prepares another plan for Jacob. Things are about to become complicated for this family.

hotspots.label: Isaac asks Esau to bring him wild game
Rebekah prepares food and uses goatskins for Jacob
Isaac can clearly see Jacob entering the room

interaction.prompt: Which details really belong in this Bible account?
interaction.accessibleAlternative: All details can be selected as labeled buttons.

progressiveHints.text: What does the Bible tell us about Isaac's eyesight?
Rebekah hears the request and makes preparations for Jacob.
Choose the request, Rebekah's preparations, and the goatskins—not Isaac seeing clearly.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 27:1–17 describes Isaac's weak eyesight, the request he makes to Esau, and Rebekah's preparations for Jacob.

discoveries.title: Esau Returns Too Late
discoveries.narration: Jacob receives Isaac's blessing while pretending to be Esau. Then Esau returns. When he learns what happened, he cries out in distress. Later he decides to kill Jacob, and Rebekah urges Jacob to leave for a time. It's a painful turn for the whole family.

left.label: What Isaac does before Esau returns

right.label: He says he is Esau, the firstborn

interaction.prompt: Connect the details that belong together.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Each pair can be selected using labeled buttons.

progressiveHints.text: Jacob answers his father's question in verse 19.
Isaac has already given the blessing when Esau arrives.
Esau's threat is recorded in verse 41.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 27:18–46 records Jacob pretending to be Esau, Isaac's blessing, Esau's reaction, and Rebekah's concern for Jacob's safety.

discoveries.title: A Promise on the Journey
discoveries.narration: Jacob leaves Beer-sheba and travels toward Haran. He stops for the night and has a remarkable dream. Jehovah reassures him and repeats the promise made to Abraham and Isaac. When Jacob wakes, he names the place Bethel.

cards.label: Jacob leaves Beer-sheba and heads toward Haran
He stops to sleep, resting his head on a stone
He dreams of a stairway and hears Jehovah's promise

interaction.prompt: Put these moments in the order the Bible gives them.
interaction.accessibleAlternative: Every event is a labeled button; no dragging required.

progressiveHints.text: Genesis 28:10 starts with Jacob's journey.
The dream happens while Jacob sleeps.
Jacob names Bethel only after waking.

discoveries.explanation: Genesis 28:10–22 describes Jacob's journey, the dream, Jehovah's promise to remain with him, and Jacob naming the place Bethel.
